explain.say: On a sunny day in Mexico City, which car is hotter inside: a black one or a silver one? The black one, by a lot! The Sun's heat reaches us as infrared radiation, which means invisible heat rays. Surfaces handle it very differently.

explain.say: Look at the left card: matt black. Matt means dull, not shiny. A matt black surface soaks up, or absorbs, most of the infrared that lands on it, so it heats up fast. Would you wear black or white on a hot day?

faq.q: Why do black surfaces get hotter in the sun?
faq.a: Matt black surfaces absorb most of the infrared radiation that hits them instead of reflecting it, so they warm up quickly.
asks: Which colour absorbs the most heat?

faq.q: Why are shiny surfaces poor at radiating heat?
faq.a: Shiny surfaces are poor emitters and poor absorbers. They reflect infrared, so they give out and take in very little.
Infrared is an invisible kind of light that carries heat. All warm objects give it out, and it can travel through empty space.

faq.q: Why can heat from the Sun cross space?
faq.a: Infrared radiation is a wave and needs no particles to travel through, unlike conduction and convection.
asks: How does the Sun heat the Earth?

faq.q: Why are fridge coils at the back often black?
faq.a: Matt black is the best emitter, so black coils give out the unwanted heat from the fridge more quickly.

facts: Matt black surfaces are the best absorbers and emitters of infrared radiation.
Shiny, light surfaces are poor absorbers and poor emitters, because they reflect infrared.

quiz.show: Which surface is the best emitter of infrared radiation?
